title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

errors: No error was found in the listed examples. All are quasi-homogeneous after a coordinate change; for case (2) this needs characteristic 0 and the extraction of roots of units in k[[x]], which is valid.

The claim x ∈ m^3 is correct in characteristic 0 as reconstructed. The note does not show how to go beyond m^3. The naive induction (x ∈ m^n for all n, then Krull intersection) is not obvious for non-graded A, because the initial forms of I mix degrees.
Transcription is uncertain in the second block, e.g. whether the hypothesis is dx = 0 in Ω_{A/k} or only modulo m. If it were only dx ∈ mΩ, the conclusion would be x ∈ m^2, not m^3.

ideas.what: Naive algebraic de Rham complex of singular or Artinian k-algebras satisfies the Poincaré lemma for quasi-homogeneous examples (cusps Y^p = x^q, double points, monomial Artinian algebras)
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré lemma for quasi-homogeneous (weighted homogeneous) singularities via the Euler vector field
ideas.usually_credited_to: Reiffen (1967, Math. Z.); K. Saito (1971, Invent. Math., converse for isolated hypersurface singularities)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966) and 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) discuss failure of the naive complex for singular schemes; these specific examples are not known to me there.

ideas.what: For A local over k (char 0) with residue field k, x ∈ m and dx = 0 imply x ∈ m^3 (injectivity of Sym^2 W → W⊗W)
ideas.modern_name: Low-order part of the statement ker(d: A → Ω_{A/k}) = k for local algebras in characteristic 0

ideas.what: Testing which singular or nilpotent algebras admit a naive Poincaré lemma, as motivation for crystalline/infinitesimal de Rham cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the naive de Rham complex vs. infinitesimal/crystalline site (Hartshorne's algebraic de Rham cohomology via formal completion)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968); On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties (1966)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's list of algebras satisfying the naive Poincaré lemma consists exactly of quasi-homogeneous examples. This anticipates in example form the Reiffen–Saito characterization (Poincaré lemma ⟺ quasi-homogeneity for isolated hypersurface singularities). The page does not state the unifying principle, and it is already well established in the literature.
missed.quote: Lemme de Poincaré vrai pour les k-algèbres suivantes (k corps de car. nulle) : k[[x]][Y]/(Y^p - x^q) ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck probing the naive de Rham complex on exactly the class later identified by Saito. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine checks: quasi-homogeneous examples where the naive Poincaré lemma holds, plus an elementary m^3 lemma. Historically mildly interesting as a probe that predates Saito's 1971 theorem, but the mathematics is standard and well documented.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Lemme de Poincaré vrai pour les' is confirmed; line 2 reads 'k-algèbres suivantes (k corps de car. nulle)'.

Second block: 'artinien' is crossed out and replaced by 'local' (the transcription's [- -]/{+ +} marking is right). The full reading is approximately 'Si A local sur k, ext. résiduelle triviale, alors pour x ∈ m avec dx = 0 [in Ω_{A/k}?], ... x ∈ m^3'. The small subscript under 'dx=0' is illegible and could be 'A/k' or 'Am'.
The reference block reads 'Ann. Éc. N. Sc. [65 ou 66] / ou J. de Liouville' with a bracket; the journal identification is a memo and remains uncertain.
